question: You soften your bench arm by lowering kp and its hand sags more. Likely cause?
options: The encoder has a constant offset from the true angle
Gravity feedforward does not match true gravity
The control loop rate is too low for this joint
explanation: A model residual is divided by kp, so a soft kp exposes it.

question: Your bench arm holds still under a PD loop with feedforward ff while true gravity is tau_g. What is the first-order steady-state error?
Your gravity model of the bench arm is lighter than the real arm. What does the arm do?
options: It droops down below the commanded angle
It floats up above the commanded angle
It holds the commanded angle exactly
explanation: Too little feedforward leaves a net downward torque.

question: You halve kp on your bench arm with the same model error. What happens to the sag?
options: It halves along with the weaker spring
It stays the same, as ff does not change
It doubles as the spring gets weaker
explanation: Sag is inversely proportional to kp.

question: On your planar bench arm, in which pose is the gravity torque on joint 1 largest?
options: Arm held out horizontal, fully stretched
Arm folded back with the elbow bent
explanation: The moment arm is the full horizontal reach when the arm is stretched out.

question: Your bench arm sags only after you lower kp. What is the best response?
options: Add integral gain on every joint to cancel it
Raise kp back up until the sag is gone
Measure sag at several poses, fix the model
explanation: Raising kp hides the model error, and integral gain adds windup and drift.
